- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and prices are trending down, model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–2% to avoid missing reversal.
- After a sharp price spike, model frequently overshoots in the immediate next period; apply a 1–3% downward correction to prevent overreaction.
- If sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish mid-horizon, model often fails to adjust; check for mean reversion in 5–7 day window and reduce forecast slope accordingly.
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to be overly optimistic in early periods (first 5–7 days); apply a 0.5–1.5% downward bias to first 5 days if sentiment is neutral or slightly bullish.
- If sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67) and price is volatile, model often fails to capture mean reversion; use 7-day moving average of true values as a sanity check for mid-horizon correction.
